newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lufthansa, Swissair to raise passenger fares.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, Swissair to raise passenger fares.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Swissair plan to raise airfares for passengers due to rising fuel costs, following earlier increases for air cargo, executives from both companies told a news conference here on Monday.
No date for the increase was set.
Lufthansa executive board chairman, Juergen Weber said," We will up charges for passengers but the amount will vary from area to area. We've had significant extra costs of more than DM 100 million."
He was speaking during the annual general meeting of the International Air Transport Association(IATA).
Swissair president, Otto Loepfe said,"We're spending $10million a month extra on fuel for cargo. We're now looking at the passenger side as well."
On October 25 Lufthansa was the first major airline to announce a cargo surcharge of 10 cents a kg or its local currency equivalent due to a rise in fuel costs estimated at 50 percent since July.
This was then followed by British Airways PLC, Air France, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV.
BA and some other airlines have also introduced increases in passenger fares.
IATA is holding an emergency meeting in Geneva on November 13 to review the impact of sharply higher jet fuel cost on both passengers and air cargo services.
The organisation's president, Pierre Jeanniot told the news conference that"fuel costs are rising rapidly, much too rapidly."
"There is a limit as to how much can be absorbed by the airlines," he added.
Asked whether fares would come down if fuel prices dropped Lufthansa's Weber said" It is not a problem. This industry is always too fast in reducing its prices."
